title: Midnight at the launch
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
arc: The Last Week of the Century
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: New Year's Eve at the boat launch. The uncle's radio counting down. Nothing happens. The tide comes in. The strip refuses to change how it writes the date.

panels.composition: The boat launch at night, the shack's half-lit string, the UNCLE in the doorway with a transistor radio, GULLY and WOOD on the dock, BARNABY between them. The bay black.

image.prompt: a boat launch at night with a shack's half-lit string of lights, an old man in the doorway holding a transistor radio, two young men and a dog on the dock over black water, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The radio. A voice drawn as a jagged balloon: a countdown as shapes.

image.prompt: close on a small transistor radio with a jagged balloon of shapes rising from it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The bay. Nothing. The tide, a little higher than before. Gully looking at Wood. Wood looking at the water.

image.prompt: a black bay at night with the tide slightly higher on the pilings, two young men on a dock looking at nothing happening, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The margin. The signature, and the date — written as the strip always wrote it, the year as two digits, the strip's own small refusal. The gull.

image.prompt: close on a comic strip's bottom margin with a small signature, a date and a two-stroke gull mark, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: A. Finch — Small Wood, OR · 12/31/99. The two-digit year, kept on purpose.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Nothing happens. The tide comes in. The date stays two digits.
